2610.05566.title: LifeLong Digital Twin: A Unified Modeling Paradigm and Agent Harness for Event-Driven Lifelong Health State Trajectories
2610.05566.paper_summary: Human health is a continuous, dynamic trajectory shaped by the cumulative interplay of biological processes, clinical events, behaviors and environmental exposures across the life course. Unifying the full breadth of lifelong health information, including longitudinal records, genetic variation, molecular profiles and environmental histories, is essential for whole-person modeling and remains a major challenge. We introduce LifeLong Digital Twin, a unified, event-driven modeling paradigm that organizes Life Events into daily Health States and accumulates them into Lifelong Health Context. An accompanying Agent Harness incorporates multimodal evidence beyond the language model's textual context. We evaluate four language models across 25 disease endpoints on three tasks: Disease Trajectory Forecasting, Disease Risk Ranking and Multi-horizon Disease Prediction. The approach yields marked gains over the reference condition: model-averaged F1 increases by 22.0% for disease identification in trajectory forecasting and 18.3% for five-year disease outcomes; thyroid-disease F1 reaches 0.669. The framework provides a foundation for whole-person digital twins and research on personalized lifelong disease prevention.
2610.05566.paper_summary_zh: 人類健康是一個持續的、動態的軌跡，受到生物過程、臨床事件、行為和環境暴露在生命過程中累積交互作用的影響。統一整個生命健康信息的全貌，包括縱向記錄、遺傳變異、分子特徵和環境歷史，對於整體人模型至關重要，並且仍然是一個主要挑戰。我們介紹了 LifeLong Digital Twin，一種統一的、事件驅動的建模範式，將生命事件組織成每日健康狀態，並將其累積成終身健康背景。隨附的 Agent Harness 包含超越語言模型文本上下文的多模態證據。我們在三個任務上評估了四種語言模型，涵蓋 25 種疾病終點：疾病軌跡預測、疾病風險排名和多時間範圍疾病預測。該方法在參考條件下產生了顯著的增益：在軌跡預測中，疾病識別的模型平均 F1 提高了 22.0%，五年疾病結果提高了 18.3%；甲狀腺疾病的 F1 達到 0.669。該框架為整體人數位雙胞胎和個性化終身疾病預防研究提供了基礎。
